units.text: After the next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to God, that I may make propitiation for your sin.”
Moses returned to the Lord and said, “I beseech Thee, O Lord: this people has committed a great sin and made themselves gods of gold.
Now, if Thou wilt forgive their sin, forgive it; but if not, blot me out of Thy book which Thou hast written.”
The Lord said to Moses, “If anyone has sinned before Me, I will blot him out of My book.

“At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.
Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.
Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.
And Moses went up to the mountain of God; and God called to him from the mountain, saying, “This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel:
‘You yourselves have seen all that I have done to the Egyptians, and I bore you as upon eagles’ wings, and brought you to Myself.
Now therefore, if you diligently listen to My voice, and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine.
And you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the sons of Israel.”
The Lord preferred you and chose you, not because you were more numerous than all the nations, for you are the fewest of all the nations,

but because the Lord loved you, and kept the oath which He sware unto your fathers, the Lord brought you forth with a mighty hand and with an uplifted arm, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, out of the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
And you shall know that the Lord your God, He is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments, unto a thousand generations,
As a father has compassion on children, the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,
for He knew our formation. Remember that we are dust.
A man—his days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so he will flower,
for a wind passed through him, and he will not exist, and he will no longer recognize his place.
But the Lord’s mercy is from eternity to eternity toward those who fear Him, and His righteousness toward children’s children,
to those who keep His covenant and remember His commandments to do them.
When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.
All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.
Then the King will say to those at His right, ‘Come, you blessed by My Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed Me,
naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’
Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry and feed Thee, or thirsty and give Thee drink?
When did we see Thee a stranger and welcome Thee, or naked and clothe Thee?
When did we see Thee sick or in prison and come to Thee?’
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’
Then He will also say to those at His left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you did not give Me food, I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink,
I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’
Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve Thee?’
Then He will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.’
And these shall depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

Therefore, as a stalk is burned by a fiery coal and consumed by a rising flame, their root will become like chaff and their blossom rise like dust. For they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.

The Lord Sabaoth was enraged with wrath against His people, brought His hand against them and struck them. The mountains were roused, and their carcasses became like dung in the middle of the road. In all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.
For just as you drank on My holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.
But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.
But the angel said to him, “Do not fear, Zechariah, for your petition has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great before the Lord. He will certainly drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
He will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

He himself will go before Him in Elijah’s spirit and power, to turn fathers’ hearts toward children and the disobedient to the understanding of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.”
